Clearly defined exceptions include emergency recovery, safety-of-flight protection, and formally delegated higher authority.
If a mission-critical input is missing, the plan shall remain incomplete and clearly indicate what still needs to be provided.
If inputs conflict, the system shall flag the conflict and block execution until it is resolved or an authorized user overrides it.
Role precedence shall follow the current mission phase and the role with the highest immediate safety or operational impact.
If the aircraft is in a critical control phase, aircraft control shall take priority over planning or distribution.
Payload operation shall not supersede aircraft control unless it is explicitly assigned and safe to do so.
Any role switch shall require either a system-confirmed handoff or an approved role change.
The system shall prevent a person from acting in two conflicting roles at once without the system knowing.
The system shall prioritize the most immediate safety-of-flight or mission-survival need at that moment.

If phases overlap or change suddenly, the system shall automatically elevate aircraft control and recovery-type actions ahead of planning, payload work, or product distribution whenever there is any conflict.
When a higher-priority control need exists, the system shall suspend or downgrade the current task until that control need is satisfied, unless an authorized exception is specifically declared.
The system shall require an explicit acknowledgment from the command-and-control side, not merely receipt of the message, before treating a tasking handoff as complete.
The system shall verify that the tasking was accepted and validated by the external side before marking the handoff complete and activating the new mission details.
If acknowledgment is not received, the system shall keep the handoff pending and alert the operator.
The system shall show a clear pending-handoff status with the reason, the elapsed wait time, and which mission elements are still not authoritative.
After a defined timeout, the system shall escalate to the operator and possibly to a supervisor or alternate channel.
The system shall not auto-complete the tasking unless this is explicitly approved by policy.
If the mission must continue, the system shall keep the previous confirmed tasking active until the new acknowledgment arrives or an authorized contingency is invoked.
